CRITICAL fixed (security, proven by running it): scripts/whatsapp-webhook-handler.py wrapped its HMAC signature check in `if APP_SECRET:`. The env-var validation that would have caught an unset secret lives under `if __name__ == "__main__"`, which never executes under a WSGI server, and gunicorn is how the endpoint is actually deployed because Meta requires HTTPS. Demonstrated: with WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET unset a forged-signature POST returned HTTP 200 and the bot processed the injected message. Now returns 500 when the secret is missing; forged 403, missing header 403, valid 200, GET verify 200/403 all re-verified.

CRITICAL fixed (security): `app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=8080, debug=True)`. The Werkzeug debugger is remote code execution by design, bound to all interfaces on a host that must be publicly reachable for Meta to deliver webhooks. Now 127.0.0.1 + debug=False with a gunicorn line.

Fixed in the copy-paste code blocks in BOTH language files (agents emit these, not scripts/): the phone regexes had no digit-boundary anchors, so the landline pattern also matched the first nine characters of an unseparated mobile and `0521234567` yielded the real number PLUS the bogus `052123456` (two numbers in, three out, one truncated). Anchored and de-duplicated. Separately `is_valid_teudat_zehut("000000000")` returned True: all-zeros passes mod-10 and is the commonest placeholder; now rejected.

Fixed (Expert, Israeli PII): a valid Teudat Zehut beginning with 0 is exactly nine digits and so is an unseparated landline, so the same string landed in BOTH `phone_numbers` and `teudat_zehut`. Anything downstream that dials an extracted number would dial a national ID, and the ID would sit in a field nobody treats as sensitive. Nine-digit runs that pass the check digit are now excluded from phone candidates.

Fixed (Expert): the Telegram scaffold's Hebrew `new_order` branch reused the `order_ask` string, so a user tapping 'הזמנה חדשה' was asked for the number of the order they were trying to create. Hebrew is the default language, so this was the path almost every user took. Added a distinct `new_order_ask` in both languages.

Fixed (Expert): the BotFather command list the skill tells you to paste advertised /status, which no handler registered (pure silence, since filters.COMMAND excludes it from the text handler), and omitted /faq, which worked. Registered /status and added faq to the published list in both language files.

Version handling made durable rather than chased: the Graph API version is now one named constant with the support window recorded (v25.0, released 18 Feb 2026, supported until 29 Jul 2028; Meta retires a version about two years after release). v26.0 exists as of 29 Jul 2026 but v25.0 is NOT stale, so the skill points at the changelog instead of pinning a number that re-stales every quarter. Telegram Bot API version confirmed as 10.3 (24 Aug 2026) and recorded in Reference Links; the skill deliberately pins no Bot API version.

Deferred (MAJOR, Expert, highest value next cycle): the webhook code block in the SKILL bodies did NOT receive the hardening that scripts/ got. It still has module-level `APP_SECRET = "your_app_secret"` literals and indexes `change["field"]` directly, which 500s on every statuses-only delivery receipt. It does fail closed on signature, so it is not an auth bypass, but it is the copy an agent actually emits.

Deferred (MAJOR, Expert): no webhook idempotency. Replaying one wamid three times produced three replies. Meta retries any webhook that is not answered fast, and all routing runs synchronously before the 200, so a slow Graph call causes the retry that causes the duplicate. A seen-message-id set plus returning 200 before dispatch is the standard shape and the skill teaches neither. Also: the in-memory session dict has no TTL or eviction and does not survive `gunicorn -w >1`.

Also: 07X numbers (10 digits, VoIP and much of Israeli business) match no phone pattern.
